name: Civil Engineering (Min)

rules.name: Prerequisite Calculus Course
rules.desc:
The minimum prerequisite for a Civil Engineering Minor, including the Civil Engineering Minor focused on Sustainable Architecture and Engineering, is MATH 19 Calculus (or MATH 20 Calculus or MATH 21 Calculus).
Students should recognize that a minor in civil engineering is not an ABET-accredited degree program.
rules.notes: Note that while not necessarily required to complete the minor, many courses of interest require PHYSICS 41 Mechanics and/or MATH 51 Linear Algebra, Multivariable Calculus, and Modern Applications as prerequisites.

rules.name: Six advisor-approved letter-graded courses of 3+ units (24 units, not taken for the major)
rules.desc:
Since undergraduates with varying backgrounds may be interested in obtaining a civil engineering minor, and the field itself is so broad, no single set of course requirements will be appropriate for all students. Instead, interested students are encouraged to propose courses within the guidelines below.
General guidelines are:

• A civil engineering minor must contain at least 24 units of coursework not taken for the major and consist of at least six classes of at least three units each of letter-graded work, except where letter grades are not offered.

• The list of courses must represent a coherent body of knowledge in a focused area and should include classes that build upon one another.

• To declare a minor with the CEE department, students must complete a Civil or Environmental Systems Engineering Minor Program form. Professor Greg Deierlein (ggd@stanford.edu) is the advisor for minors in Civil Engineering. Catherine Gorle (gorle@stanford.edu) is the advisor for minors in the CE Sustainable Architecture and Engineering track. Students must consult with the appropriate advisor in developing their minor program, obtain the advisor’s approval (including signature) of their study list on the CE Minor Program Sheet, and email to the CEE Assistant Director of Undergraduate Degree Progress, Rachel Stringari (rstring@stanford.edu).

• Two quarters prior to graduation, the student should meet with the Assistant Director of UG Degree Progress to review their course plan for graduation.

• Minors must be officially declared and all courses completed (or in progress) no later than the deadline for a student’s application to graduate.

rules.name: Cumulative GPA of 2.0 in the minor courses

gpa: Cumulative GPA for all minor courses must be at least 2.0.
grading: Complete at least six classes of at least three units each of letter-graded work, except where letter grades are not offered.
policies: Coursework used toward Civil Engineering Minor requirements may not be double-counted to fulfill major or other minor program requirements.
transferPolicy: Transfer credit petitions are reviewed case by case and must be approved by both the School of Engineering and the Civil and Environmental Engineering department.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the calculus prerequisite (MATH 19, 20 or 21). The minor has no fixed course list: you move in six advisor-approved courses of at least three units each, letter graded where offered, for at least 24 units not used for your major or another minor. The prerequisite does not count toward the 24 units. You check the 2.0 GPA and the advisor-signed program sheet by hand.
